stapel under BMAD (2026-11-04, the human, in the chat; research in .stapel/scratch/bmad-research-2026-11-04.md and bmad-vision-2026-11-04.md). The vision changes: stapel is the verification and measurement layer under a pluggable method, BMAD first; pain 1 becomes keeping software alive at a known cost, pain 2 is split into what the organisation knows (the method) and the unchecked sum of changes (stapel). The scheme: one planning session with BMAD only (Sofia writes the initiative, the epics and tickets.toml; the human approves the breakdown; the session ends with a recommended /clear), then build sessions with stapel only that consume the BMAD files. Two new plan items, taken after STP-27 closes and after the BMAD v7.0.0 tag, before the pilot: (a) stapel next without a key reads id and after from tickets.toml, with the field names in stapel.toml, tolerant of unknown fields, a warning on a missing one, and prints new-ticket from entry; the orchestrator reads the epic and the entry as text and writes the Frame, the criteria with R ids and the Decisions log; stapel close prints the phrase mark story done as its last line; a contract test on the two fields; (b) the skill gets the rule: after a BMAD planning session a new session for each ticket, no BMAD skill in a build session. Dropped from stapel's own plan: an epic to tickets stage, context authoring in 3.1 (stapel reads and enforces the block bmad-project-context writes), bug and spike templates in 3.6, a tracker adapter; phase 3 narrows to the guards folder, the ratchet, the API snapshot and the dependency dialog; levels 1 and 2 stay, level 3 stays after the guards. Unchanged: guard, check, lint, ship, tokens, findings, ledger, index, the leaf contract and the spec reviewer. Reason: BMAD is maintained by about a hundred authors and the human cannot keep up by borrowing; stapel keeps the part BMAD's form cannot give. docs/PLAN.md section 1 and docs/PHASES.md are updated by decision 0005 after STP-27.

Phases after the gate and the feature level (2026-11-10, the human, in the chat). Replaces the decision 'stapel under BMAD' of 2026-11-04. Reason: two systems double the elaboration (the method writes a ticket, then the stapel orchestrator rewrites it into the Frame and the criteria and asks again), need two installs (Python through uv and Node beside one binary) and two state stores, and the method's story format broke compatibility in 10 of 12 minor releases; decisions 0001 to 0003 already took ideas from that method the same way. Decided: (1) stapel gets its own feature level, optional, two levels only (feature, ticket): a feature is a ticket of kind feature with a description, requirements with ids, a Decisions log and a breakdown into tickets with dependencies; it has no build and no status of its own, its readiness is computed from its tickets. (2) The elaboration texts (questions, template, checklists) are ported from the method's repository into the skill stapel init installs; its licence is MIT (checked 2026-11-10): the copyright and permission notice is kept, and the method's name is a trademark, used only in a truthful compatibility statement, never in the product name or marketing; no tracker stores, no personas, no Python tooling are taken; a report per release of the method lists ideas worth taking. (3) Staleness goes from the feature to its tickets: a ticket records the hash of each requirement it covers; a changed requirement makes an unbuilt ticket wait for a new confirmation, stops a ticket in build, and marks a closed ticket as built against the old text until the human decides. (4) stapel measures the quality of a feature spec by three numbers per ticket: intent_gap findings and questions (enough information), brief size and builder tokens (not too much), dialogs and the human's minutes (attention). (5) The editor: no extension and no LSP; the human page is written to a file the person opens in the editor, and the dialog shows a short summary bound to the page's hash. (6) Item 1.14 (A3) widens by two pilot measures: the time from a confirmation request to its answer, and the count of questions that concern the feature, not the ticket. (7) If the gate (2.4) passes, the phases are taken in this order, chosen by the human: phase 3, one ticket made lighter: 3.1 the human page as a file, 3.2 stapel check in CI of the repository; phase 4, the feature level: 4.1 the elaboration skill, 4.2 kind feature with the breakdown and child tickets, 4.3 staleness from requirements to tickets, 4.4 computed readiness; phase 5, the sum of changes: 5.1 the guards folder with ratchet baselines run by check and CI, 5.2 the dependency dialog and the public API snapshot. The pilot's findings may reorder them only by a ledger decision. Still candidates without a place in the order: lint, ship, guard items 1.9 and 1.10, an import from the method or from a tracker when a real user asks, the index, autonomy levels, an editor extension, more languages, removal of the empty crates, one short plan document. The business model changes with it: the method is a source of ideas and a possible input, not the upper layer of stapel.

Two stapel checks of parallel tickets work badly together (the human, 2026-11-11, seen in STP-29 beside STP-28). The check lock is one for the repository and all its worktrees, and a second check is refused at once (another stapel check runs) instead of waiting, so the session must retry by hand: twice in STP-29. When it is not refused it waits behind the machine-wide cargo lock: three full checks of STP-29 took over ten minutes of waiting each. Both checks build into one check-target folder in the git common folder, which is why the lock is shared. With a full check after every builder commit, parallel tickets are parallel in writing and serial in checking. Candidates: the check waits for the check lock as stapel cargo waits for its lock; a check-target per worktree; a full check only before code review and before the close, with check --history after each commit (the proposal of 2026-10-22 that was withdrawn).
